front: How much a quantity grew or shrank, as a percent of where it started.
cue: Any "by what percent did it change" question.
trap: Brackets around the difference, divide by the OLD value, then × 100. A fall comes out negative.

front: A percent of a quantity.
cue: Energy passed on, water lost, the share of a budget.
trap: Turn the percent into a decimal first: 10% is 0.10. "40% less" means 60% is left.

front: Growth from births and deaths, when both rates are per 1,000 people.
cue: Turning crude birth and death rates into a growth rate in percent.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>rate of natural increase </mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{rate of natural increase }(\%)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>CBR</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>CDR</mtext></mrow><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{CBR} - \text{CDR}}{10}</annotation></semantics></math>
worked: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{30 - 10}{10}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo>%</mo><mtext> per year</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2.0\,\%\text{ per year}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Divide by 10, not 100: the rates are per 1,000.

front: Growth from counts, with migration: B births, I immigrants, D deaths, E emigrants.
cue: When the scenario gives numbers of people rather than rates.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>growth </mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{growth }(\%)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>B</mtext><mo>+</mo><mtext>I</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>D</mtext><mo>+</mo><mtext>E</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mtext>population</mtext></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{(\text{B} + \text{I}) - (\text{D} + \text{E})}{\text{population}} \times 100</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Immigration adds, emigration subtracts; divide by the population at the start.

front: The rule of 70: how long a population (or anything growing at a steady rate) takes to double.
cue: A growth rate in percent per year, and a question about doubling.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>doubling time</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{doubling time}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mfrac><mn>70</mn><mrow><mtext>growth rate </mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx \frac{70}{\text{growth rate }(\%)}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Use the rate in percent (2, not 0.02).

front: The calendar year a population doubles.
cue: Any question that asks "in what year".
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>year it doubles</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{year it doubles}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mtext>start year</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \text{start year}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><mn>70</mn><mrow><mtext>growth rate </mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo>%</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{70}{\text{growth rate }(\%)}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Add the doubling time to the start year; 50 years is not the answer to "in what year".

front: A population after a number of doubling times.
cue: How big something gets after a stated time at a steady growth rate.
trap: Count the doublings first: t divided by the doubling time.

front: Exponential growth at r percent a year, year by year.
cue: A projection a set number of years ahead.
trap: r is a percent, so divide by 100; t is the exponent, not a multiplier.

front: Replacement-level fertility: the average number of children per woman that keeps a population the same size over time.
cue: Judging whether a population will grow or shrink in the long run.
worked: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.4 - 2.1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>children per woman above 2.1</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.3\,\text{children per woman above 2.1}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Not 2.0: a little extra makes up for children who do not survive to have children.

front: Total fertility rate from birth rates in 5-year age bands.
cue: A table of births per 1,000 women by age group.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>TFR</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{TFR}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>sum of age-specific birth rates per 1,000 women</mtext><mo>×</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{sum of age-specific birth rates per 1,000 women} \times 5}{1{,}000}</annotation></semantics></math>
worked: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>110</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>130</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(20 + 110 + 130 + 90 + 40 + 10 + 0) \times 5}{1{,}000}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>children per woman</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2.0\,\text{children per woman}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Multiply by the 5 years in each band, then divide by 1,000.

front: Net primary productivity: the energy producers store, after their own respiration.
cue: What is left for consumers, from GPP and respiration.
trap: NPP is never larger than GPP; GPP = NPP + respiration.

front: The 10% rule: about a tenth of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next.
cue: Energy at the top of a food chain from the energy at the bottom.
trap: Multiply by 0.10 once per arrow: producers to secondary consumers is two steps, × 0.01.

front: The share of input energy that comes out as useful work.
cue: Power plants, engines, light bulbs.
trap: Output over input, never the other way round.

front: Efficiencies in a chain multiply.
cue: Fuel to plant to wires to motor.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>overall efficiency</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{overall efficiency}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>×</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>×</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>×</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e_1 \times e_2 \times e_3 \times \ldots</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Multiply the decimals; do not add or average the percents.

front: Energy used by a device running at a steady power.
cue: Electricity use from wattage and hours.
trap: Watts to kilowatts: divide by 1,000.

front: What a quantity costs.
cue: Electricity, water or fuel bills.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>cost</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{cost}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mtext>quantity</mtext><mo>×</mo><mtext>price per unit</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \text{quantity} \times \text{price per unit}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Keep the units: kWh × <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>W</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">/kWh gives</annotation></semantics></math>; multiply, do not divide by the price.

front: Money (or energy) saved by a change.
cue: An upgrade, a new bulb, a new irrigation method.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>savings</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{savings}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>use before</mtext><mo>−</mo><mtext>use after</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mtext>price</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (\text{use before} - \text{use after}) \times \text{price}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Subtract first, then multiply; the cost of the new use alone is not the saving.

front: Carbon dioxide (or another gas) released, from how much fuel or electricity is used.
cue: Emissions, or emissions saved by a change.
trap: The factor's units must cancel what you multiply: kWh × kg CO₂/kWh.

front: Unit conversion by dimensional analysis: each factor is a fraction equal to 1.
cue: Gallons to liters, hectares to square meters, BTU to kWh, and any chain of them.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>value in new unit</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{value in new unit}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mtext>value</mtext><mo>×</mo><mfrac><mtext>new unit</mtext><mtext>old unit</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \text{value} \times \frac{\text{new unit}}{\text{old unit}}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Put the unit you want to get rid of in the denominator, so it cancels.

front: How many times a radioactive or breaking-down substance has halved.
cue: The first step of every half-life question.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>number of half-lives</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{number of half-lives}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>time</mtext><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{time}}{t_{1/2}}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Divide the time by the half-life, not the other way round.

front: What is left after time t.
cue: Radioactive decay, or a pesticide breaking down.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>amount left</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{amount left}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mtext>amount</mtext><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \text{amount} \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / t_{1/2}}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Three half-lives leave one eighth, not one third or one sixth.

front: The dose that kills half of a test population, read off a dose-response curve.
cue: Comparing how toxic two substances are.
worked: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>dose at </mtext><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo><mtext> deaths</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{dose at }50\%\text{ deaths}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>20</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>mg/kg</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 20\,\text{mg/kg}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: A lower LD50 means a MORE toxic substance; read across from 50% to the curve, then down to the dose.

front: A whole-body dose from a dose in mg per kg.
cue: How much of a substance would reach a stated dose.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>dose</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{dose}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mtext>dose per kg</mtext><mo>×</mo><mtext>body mass (kg)</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \text{dose per kg} \times \text{body mass (kg)}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Convert body mass to kilograms first.

front: Biomagnification: concentration multiplies by a factor at each step up a food chain.
cue: The concentration in a top predator.
trap: Bioaccumulation is one organism over time; biomagnification is up the chain.

front: How many times more concentrated a substance is at one level than another.
cue: "How many times greater" questions, and comparing LD50s.
trap: Divide, do not subtract; the answer has no unit ("times").

front: An amount per person.
cue: Water use, energy use, waste or footprint per person.
worked: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4.5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>9</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>L</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>people</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4.5 \times 10^{9}\,\text{L}}{3 \times 10^{6}\,\text{people}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mtext>L per person</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1{,}500\,\text{L per person}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Scale words first: 4.5 billion is 4,500,000,000.

front: How crowded a population is.
cue: People per square kilometer, trees per hectare.
trap: Area units must match the question (km² or hectares).

front: Irrigation water from the depth applied and the field area.
cue: Water applied to a field or stored in a wetland.
trap: Put depth and area in matching units (m and m²) before you multiply.

front: Water use per hectare (or per acre).
cue: Comparing irrigation methods or farms of different sizes.
formula: <math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mtext>water per area</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{water per area}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="env-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mtext>volume</mtext><mtext>area</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\text{volume}}{\text{area}}</annotation></semantics></math>
trap: Volume over area, and keep both units in the answer (m³/ha).
